reading.body:
DFW29 publishes 100,000 square feet of technical space and no IT load figure in megawatts, placing it outside the measurable set of Texas facilities tracked for AI infrastructure scaling.

Because no power number is published, no rack or accelerator estimate can be derived. The absence of a megawatt figure means this campus does not contribute to the 389 MW total recorded for Texas facilities that do disclose power consumption. Without power data, the facility's relevance to AI compute capacity cannot be assessed, regardless of its physical footprint.

The three certifications listed qualify the campus for specific workloads. PCI DSS, ISO 27001, and ISO 9001 establish compliance frameworks for payment processing, information security, and quality management respectively. None of these certifications is specific to AI infrastructure, and none implies the power densities that large-scale AI training or inference typically demands.

DFW29 occupies a meaningful 100,000 square feet in the Dallas concentration, one of Texas's densest data center regions. Whether it carries AI workloads, who its tenants are, and what its actual power draw is remain unknown from the operator's published specifications. A facility of this size could matter to the grid constraint on AI scaling, but only if its power consumption were disclosed.
